items.title: Tannin Phenology is Associated with the Timing of Asiatic Black Bear Foraging among Persimmon Fruit Types
items.authors: D. Fujiki
items.abstract: This study examined whether variation in tannin concentrations and tannin insolubilization timing among persimmon fruit types influences foraging frequency and seasonal timing in Asiatic black bears (Ursus thibetanus). Bear-constructed feeding platforms in persimmon trees served as fruit consumption indicators. The probability of platform formation was highest in pollination-constant nonastringent (PCNA) persimmons, intermediate in pollination-variant nonastringent (PVNA) fruit, and lower in pollination-variant astringent (PVA) and pollination-constant astringent (PCA) types. Platform formation timing followed a similar sequence, occurring earliest in PCNA, then PVNA, and subsequently PVA and PCA persimmons. Soluble phenolic content, a proxy for tannin concentration, was measured in fruit collected immediately after platform formation. Bear feeding platform formation was observed mainly at relatively low soluble phenolic levels, generally below approximately 0.5% fresh weight (FW) tannic acid equivalents (TAE). Generalized additive models describing seasonal changes in soluble phenolic concentrations indicated that concentrations were highest in PCA, followed by PVA, PVNA, and PCNA persimmons. The decline to low concentrations occurred earliest in PCNA and progressively later through PVNA, PVA, and PCA types. Overall, these findings suggest that soluble phenolic concentration and its seasonal dynamics may be associated with the temporal patterns of bear foraging on persimmon fruit.

items.title: Identification of key chestnut-sweet aroma compounds in bud-leaf yellow tea and analysis of their dynamic changes and formation mechanism.
items.authors: Jing-Tao Zhou, Lu-Qi Bi, Qing-Ning Shu, Xing-Ping Zhang, Tong-Tong Jia, De Zhang
items.abstract: Bud-leaf yellow tea is known for its chestnut-sweet aroma, yet its key odorants and formation mechanism remain unclear. Using a sensomics approach, seven key odorants were characterized, including 2-ethyl-3,5-dimethylpyrazine, 3-methylbutanal, and dimethyl sulfide, with 2-ethyl-3,5-dimethylpyrazine being the major contributor (recombination correlation r = 0.909). 2-Ethyl-3,5-dimethylpyrazine (odor activity value = 53.3, flavor dilution = 1024) and dimethyl sulfide (odor activity value = 422.4, flavor dilution = 256) were identified as major contributors, with dimethyl sulfide dominating the chestnut note and 2-Ethyl-3,5-dimethylpyrazine enhancing the sweet dimension. Across Meizhan, FudingDabaicha and Echa 10, 2-ethyl-3,5-dimethylpyrazine was undetectable before yellowing, peaked during yellowing (14.92 μg/L, p < 0.05), and was moisture-dependent, with 25% post-fixation moisture giving the highest chestnut-sweet score. In vitro, β-alanine + D-arabinose produced 2-ethyl-3,5-dimethylpyrazine via the Maillard reaction. Thus, 2-ethyl-3,5-dimethylpyrazine is the yellowing-specific key chestnut-sweet odorant in bud-leaf yellow tea, enabling moisture-based process control.

items.title: Windthrow of Forest Trees and Its Effect on Tree Regeneration and Diversity of Understory in the Hyrcanian Temperate Upland Forests of Iran
items.authors: B. Kiani, Sharare Behbudi, Mehrdad Nikooy, A. Omidi
items.abstract: Windthrow is a major natural disturbance shaping canopy dynamics in temperate forests, yet high-elevation (upland) Hyrcanian forests remain poorly studied, particularly with respect to regeneration responses and topographic controls. This study examined windfall effects in Dashte Daman forests, northern Iran (1027–1629 m elevation). First, 90 systematically distributed 50 × 50 m sample plots were established across a 300 × 300 m grid on a stratified map including affected and unaffected areas. For each fallen tree (broken or uprooted), diameter at breast height, trunk height, and crown length were measured. Understory vegetation composition, including herbaceous cover and tree regeneration, was also recorded. The influence of topographic variables (slope, elevation, aspect) and forest type on windfall abundance was analyzed, alongside correlations with slope, elevation, distance to nearest road, stand density, and canopy cover. Comparisons with undisturbed control areas were made to assess regeneration patterns. Results indicated that oriental beech (Fagus orientalis) was the most windfall species, followed by common hornbeam (Carpinus betulus), whereas chestnut-leaved oak (Quercus castaneifolia) and common ash (Fraxinus excelsior) were rare. Windfall frequency averaged eight fallen and 4.7 uprooted (a total of 12.7) trees per hectare, with corresponding volumes of 31.6 m3/ha and 18.56 m3/ha, respectively. Considering the abundance of wind-fallen trees, windfall frequency was highest on south-, southwest-, and west-aspects, at slopes of 20%–40%, and elevations of 1000–1200 m. Valleys exhibited greater tree breakage, whereas uprooting dominated hillsides. Pure oriental beech stands had significantly higher windfall rates than mixed beech-hornbeam or oak-hornbeam forests.…

items.title: From Textile Waste Toward a Leather Alternative: Mechanical and Abrasion Performance of Polycaprolactone-Reinforced Reclaimed Nonwoven Cotton
items.authors: Bahar Hashemian Esfahani, S. Dutta, R. Eike, Boyce S. Chang, Zahra Falsafi, Manu Smriti
items.abstract: Transforming textile waste into durable, value-added materials remains a central challenge for sustainable apparel systems. This study developed single-layer, nonwoven sheets from discarded 100% cotton textiles using a papermaking-derived wet-laid process and evaluated their potential as leather-alternative materials through a sequential two-phase approach. In Phase 1, reclaimed-cotton nonwoven sheets bio-finished with persimmon juice or konjac were benchmarked against commercial plant-based olive, cork, pineapple, and cactus leather alternatives using ASTM grab tensile and rotary-platform abrasion testing. The bio-finished sheets showed low breaking forces, limited elongation, and abrasion failure. In Phase 2, biodegradable polycaprolactone (PCL) was applied as a reinforcing finish. The resulting PCL-treated reclaimed-cotton sheets’ (RC-PCL) breaking force performance improved by over 6.5 times the nontreated nonwoven specimens and approximately 4.5 times the bio-finished nonwoven specimens. Additionally, the RC-PCL completed the 2000-cycle abrasion endpoint without through-thickness failure. Elongation remained low while the dogbone tensile test showed increases in tensile strength, strain at break, and apparent Young’s modulus after PCL-finishing. These findings indicate that biodegradable PCL-finish substantially improves the strength, cohesion, and abrasion resistance of reclaimed-cotton nonwovens, while flexibility, coating optimization, and end-of-life performance remain priorities for future leather-alternative applications to support sustainability efforts and value-added use of reclaimed materials within the textile industry.

items.title: Photocatalytic treatment of AO7 and real textile wastewater using green-synthesized ZnO nanoparticles: RSM and Taguchi approach.
items.authors: S. Turkoglu, R. A. Kepekçi, O. Keskinkan
items.abstract: In this study, ZnO nanoparticles were synthesized via a green synthesis method using Diospyros kaki L. peel extract, and their photocatalytic performances for the removal of Acid Orange 7 (AO7) dye and real textile wastewater were investigated. The effects of pH, initial dye concentration, and catalyst dosage on AO7 removal were optimized using a Box-Behnken experimental design and Response Surface Methodology (RSM). Under the optimum conditions (pH 10, initial dye concentration of 10 ppm, and catalyst dosage of 0.13 g), 100% dye removal was achieved within 270 min. The photocatalytic treatment of real textile wastewater was optimized using a Taguchi experimental design, and a color removal efficiency of 98.1% was achieved under the optimum conditions (pH 7, constant wastewater volume of 50 mL, and catalyst dosage of 0.13 g). Additionally, radical scavenging experiments performed to elucidate the photocatalytic mechanism indicated that hydroxyl radicals (•OH) play a significant role in the photocatalytic degradation of AO7. The synthesized ZnO nanoparticles exhibited high photocatalytic stability, good reusability and acted as efficient photocatalysts even under low-energy UV light conditions. Overall, the green-synthesized ZnO nanoparticles demonstrated promising potential as an effective photocatalyst for the removal of dyes and color from real textile wastewater.

items.title: Fosetyl-Al stem injection for chestnut ink disease management: efficacy and dose-dependent phytotoxicity in saplings
items.authors: P. Serrano-Pérez, G. Moreno, Mikel Cebadero, M. C. Rodríguez-Molina
items.abstract: Fosetyl-Al (aluminium tris-(ethyl phosphonate)) is a low-toxicity phosphonate commonly used to control oomycete-related diseases in crops. Trunk injection (endotherapy) delivers the fungicide directly into the vascular system, potentially improving efficacy while reducing off-target losses. This two-year study evaluated the efficacy and phytotoxicity of stem-injected fosetyl-Al to manage ink disease caused by Phytophthora cinnamomi in Castanea sativa saplings. Fifty saplings received fosetyl-Al injections at 0–4% using pressurized devices, followed by stem inoculation with the pathogen; a 2% soil irrigation treatment was included for comparison. Stem injections at 1%, 2% and 4% significantly suppressed stem necrosis after inoculation with P. cinnamomi and reduced root infections compared to irrigation and untreated control. Protection persisted for at least two years as reflected by reduced relative Area Under the Disease Progress Curve (rAUDPC) values. However, stem injections also induced phytotoxic symptoms, including leaf burn, necrosis, and occasional plant death, with a clear dose-dependent relationship. Most plants recovered from moderate phytotoxicity, whereas irreversible damage occurred at the highest doses, highlighting the critical need for precise dose adjustments, particularly in small-diameter trees. Logistic regression identified a Minimum Effective Dose (MED) range of 0.061–0.102 g/cm (a.i.) of stem circumference, corresponding to predicted disease incidence thresholds of < 10% to < 1%, respectively, with associated phytotoxicity risks of approximately 10–25%. These results indicate that trunk injection of fosetyl-Al can provide effective and targeted control of ink disease in young chestnut plants under the conditions tested, while emphasizing the need…

items.title: Comparative Evaluation of Physicochemical Properties, Bioactive Compounds and Chemometric Discrimination of Honey Samples from Different Botanical and Geographical Origins
items.authors: Arleta Rifati-Nixha, M. Dërmaku-Sopjani, Mustafa Arslan, Edlira Riza, Ariona Lubishtani
items.abstract: The chemical and quality characteristics of honey vary considerably according to floral source, geographical provenance, environmental conditions, and post-harvest handling, complicating its characterization and authentication. In this study, physicochemical properties, bioactive constituents, enzymatic activity, and exploratory chemometric patterns were evaluated in thirteen honey samples representing different declared botanical types, including sage, meadow, chestnut, acacia, and pine honeys, from different geographical origins. Physicochemical characterization comprised moisture content, refractive index, specific optical rotation, electrical conductivity, pH, free acidity, hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF), reducing sugars, ash content, qualitative mineral composition, and preliminary authenticity-related tests. Total phenolic content determined by the Folin–Ciocalteu assay (TPC-FC), total flavonoid content (TFC), total phenolic content determined by the Prussian Blue assay (TPC-PB), proline content, and diastase activity were also evaluated. Statistical analysis included one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) followed by Tukey’s HSD test, Pearson correlation analysis, and principal component analysis (PCA). One-way ANOVA followed by Tukey’s HSD test indicated significant differences in the measured analytical responses among the individual honey samples for the evaluated bioactive parameters (p < 0.05); these comparisons were restricted to the investigated samples and were not interpreted as inferential differences among botanical or geographical populations. Pearson correlation analysis revealed several moderate-to-strong associations among the analytical variables; however, none remained statistically significant after Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) corre…

items.title: Accumulation of two distinct alleles causes astringency loss in cultivated polyploid persimmon
items.authors: Fujiwara Y, Nishiyama S, Onoue N, Matsuzaki R, Kono A, Azuma A, Saito T, Shimizu T, Sato A, Ichino T, Yamane H, Yonemori K, Tao R.
items.abstract: Persimmon fruit accumulates high levels of proanthocyanidins (PAs), causing extreme astringency. In pollination-constant and non-astringent (PCNA) cultivars, PA accumulation ceases early in fruit development. Although the PCNA trait is recessively controlled by the ASTRINGENCY ( AST ) locus, its causal gene has remained unknown. Using haplotype-resolved forward genetics in a hexaploid genetic background, we identified the previously uncharacterized TANNIN ( TAN ) as the causal gene. Long-read sequencing revealed that PCNA originated through the accumulation of independently derived ast alleles that cause transcriptional deficiency of TAN . These findings resolve the complex genetic basis of natural astringency loss in persimmon and provide a framework for molecular breeding. Further investigation of TAN function would uncover mechanisms underlying massive accumulation of PAs in persimmon fruit and insight into specialized metabolite sequestration.

items.title: Adding Geographical Indication Protection to a Regional Collective Trademark: Evidence on Rural Production and Commercialisation in Japan
items.authors: Matsui K.
items.abstract: Abstract This study examines whether Geographical Indication (GI) registration generates additional changes in rural production and commercialisation when a regional product is already protected by a Regional Collective Trademark (RCT). Using Ichida Gaki, a traditional dried persimmon from Nagano Prefecture, Japan, as a case, the study compares the RCT-only period (2007–2015) with the combined RCT-plus-GI period (2017–2023). A prefecture-year panel is analysed using two-way fixed-effects models, event-study analyses, and spatial analyses. Relative to comparison prefectures, production volume remained comparatively higher after GI registration, while shipment volume and shipment rate declined. The decline in shipment volume received the strongest empirical support and remained robust across alternative specifications, whereas pre-treatment trends limit causal interpretation for production volume and shipment rate. Spatial analyses also indicate geographically heterogeneous post-registration changes among other dried-persimmon-producing prefectures. The findings suggest that GI registration may affect rural production systems not only through brand protection but also through changes in commercialisation and institutional governance. More broadly, the study highlights the importance of evaluating layered intellectual property protection as an institutional component of rural development policy whose implications may differ across production and market participation.

items.title: Winter injury of red raspberry ( Rubus idaeus L.) buds under commercial field conditions: Relationships with temperature, spur blight and biochemical traits
items.authors: Maire Tõrra, H. Kaldmäe, P. Põldma, I. Reile, Kärolin Kork, A. Kikas
items.abstract: Winter injury limits raspberry ( Rubus idaeus L.) production in northern climates. This study evaluated the associations between winter injury, temperature, spur blight severity, and bud proline and soluble sugars contents in ‘Glen Ample’ raspberry grown in eight commercial plantations in Estonia over three winters: 2021/22, 2022/23, and 2023/24. Bud injury ranged from 18 to 98% among plantations and years, while neither minimum temperature nor the maximum number of consecutive hours below −25 °C accounted for this variation. A significant positive correlation was found between spur blight ( Xenodidymella applanata ) severity and winter injury ( r = 0.833). Proline and soluble carbohydrate levels in March were not consistent indicators of bud winter survival. These findings demonstrate that winter injury of raspberry buds is determined by interacting abiotic and biotic stress factors rather than by minimum temperature alone and growers should consider cane health alongside winter temperature in winter-injury risk assessments.

items.title: Dissecting the genetic basis of DUS characters in Pakistani wheat varieties
items.authors: Haq IU, Qureshi IA, Hussain MA, Javaid RA, Sheikh F, Abbas Z, Azam M.
items.abstract: Distinctness, Uniformity and Stability (DUS) testing is fundamental to varietal characterization and the protection of Plant Breeders’ Rights (PBRs), but conventional DUS assessment relies predominantly on morphological characteristics whose expression may be influenced by environmental conditions, developmental stage and observer-related variation. Integrating character-specific molecular markers with conventional DUS assessment may therefore improve the reproducibility and genetic resolution of varietal identification. This study investigated the genetic architecture of DUS characteristics in a panel of 102 historical and modern Pakistani wheat varieties using genome-wide association studies (GWAS). Phenotypic variation was evaluated using distribution, correlation and hierarchical clustering analyses, while the germplasm was genotyped using a wheat genotyping-by-targeted sequencing platform. After quality filtering, 21,670 high-quality single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) were retained for analyses of genetic diversity, population structure, linkage disequilibrium (LD) and marker-trait associations. Population structure analysis indicated extensive admixture, with cross-entropy supporting K = 9 ancestral components, whereas hierarchical genetic clustering separated the germplasm into five broad groups. The first three principal components explained 8.09%, 7.20% and 5.39% of the total genetic variation, respectively. GWAS using BLINK and FarmCPU identified significant associations for several diagnostically important DUS characteristics. Growth habit was strongly associated with SNP 1B_129176704, with an additional signal on chromosome 5B. items.title: Traditional Plant Knowledge across Rural and Peri-Urban Istanbul: Documented Plants and Uses
items.authors: Emine Akalın, Rabia Ebrar Akıncı, Aybüke Kızılırmaklı Demir, O. Demir, E. Cabi
items.abstract: Purpose: This study examines traditional plant knowledge in rural and peri-urban Istanbul, where environmental access, household production and metropolitan connections coexist.Method: Fieldwork within Türkiye’s national programme for documenting traditional knowledge associated with bio-logical diversity covered 30 neighbourhoods in ten districts in 2021–2022. Purposive selection and local referrals iden-tified 112 informants contributing 667 plant-use reports. Original descriptions were retained alongside standardized taxonomic and use fields. Analyses examined repertoire composition, citation frequency, multifunctionality and district overlap. Retrospective taxon-level classifications distinguished predominantly wild-gathered from cultivated, managed, planted or otherwise obtained taxa, and identified a conservative subset confirmed in Istanbul flora sources. District overlap was assessed using an informant-block permutation model; sampling-adequacy estimates were exploratory.Findings: The repertoire comprises 174 taxa in 129 genera and 52 families, spanning 52 use categories, 25 plant-part groups and 12 preparation groups. Food accounted for 55.2% of reports, human health for 22.3% and household and material uses for 11.8%. Fruit and aerial parts predominated; cooking and raw use were the leading preparations. Tilia tomentosa led food citations, Olea europaea health and Castanea sativa household and material uses. The null model largely reproduced the raw increase in district overlap from taxa to preparations. Lower-than-expected preparation over-lap did not survive multiple-testing correction. items.title: Formation of a chestnut-like aroma by blending fresh-scented and bean-scented green teas.
items.authors: Yi-Jun Wang, Ya-Ya Yu, Huan Sun, Qing-Qing Cao, Fang Wang, Jian-Yong Zhang
items.abstract: Chestnut-like aroma is a favorable quality attribute of green tea. This study developed chestnut-like tea by blending fresh-scented Anji white tea (AJWT) with bean-scented Longjing green tea (LJGT). Sensory evaluation showed that increasing LJGT shifted the dominant aroma from fresh to chestnut-like and then bean-like, with 40% LJGT producing the most pronounced chestnut-like character. GC-O-MS combined with variable importance in projection (VIP) and relative odor activity value analyses (rOAVs) identified 13 key differential aroma-active compounds (VIP > 1; rOAV >1) among 137 volatiles, representing fresh, floral, and roasty notes. Aroma reconstitution associated the chestnut-like character with an rOAV-based distribution of approximately 75% fresh, 19% floral, and 6% roasty compounds. Addition experiments further suggested that cis-3-hexenyl hexanoate, β-myrcene, ethyl hexanoate, β-ionone, 2-pentylfuran, and 3-methylbutanal were associated with the aroma transition from fresh to chestnut-like. These findings support targeted regulation and blending of chestnut-like green tea aroma.

items.title: Agro-morphological Characterisation of Rice (Oryza sativa L.) Germplasm Accessions Using DUS Descriptors
items.journal: Plant cell biotechnology and molecular biology
items.authors: Priya Gupta, D. Gauraha, Jyoti Sahu
items.abstract: The present investigation was undertaken to characterise 200 rice germplasm accessions, along with seven checks, for visually assessed DUS (Distinctness, Uniformity and Stability) traits. The 207 entries were evaluated during Kharif 2020 in an augmented design with four blocks at the Research cum Instructional Farm, Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, College of Agriculture, Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya, Raipur (Chhattisgarh), at a spacing of 20 cm × 15 cm with the recommended package of practices under normal irrigated conditions (no drought stress was imposed). Observations were recorded on twenty-four DUS descriptors. Of these, one descriptor (shape of ligule) was monomorphic, nine were dimorphic and fourteen were polymorphic. Based on the Shannon–Weaver diversity index, hull colour, flag leaf attitude, panicle exsertion, grain breadth and basal leaf sheath colour were the most variable descriptors. Unique accessions such as IC390636 (aromatic) and IC516693 (red lemma) were identified, which may be useful as donors and in candidate variety development. The study provides a morphological baseline for future drought-stress evaluation; drought tolerance itself was not assessed

items.title: Seasonal hypoxia and nitrate depletion in water chestnut (Trapa natans) beds: Implications for nitrogen cycling.
items.authors: Simmons W, Blossey B, Walter MT.
items.abstract: Dense beds of floating macrophytes can alter water quality by modifying dissolved oxygen (DO) and nitrogen (N) dynamics. Water chestnut (Trapa natans L.), a non-native annual macrophyte, forms extensive seasonal beds in freshwater systems in North America. The species is intensively managed to reduce negative impacts on native species, yet its effects on DO and nitrate (NO 3 - ) remain poorly studied. We quantified DO and NO 3 - -N concentrations inside and outside of three riverine T. natans beds in New York over three growing seasons. In addition, we assessed denitrification using field-collected water and sediment in laboratory microcosm incubations. During summer months, DO of water from within T. natans beds was 76% lower on average (1.28 mg L - 1 ) compared to outside beds (5.43 mg L - 1 ). For NO 3 - -N, concentrations averaged 0.45 (2017) and 0.11 (2018) mg L - 1 outside beds, but were depleted to 0.10 (2017) and 0.01 (2018) mg L - 1 within beds, 77%-88% lower than outside beds. In 2018, 60% of samples, mostly from within beds of T. natans, were below the analytical detection limit of NO 3 - -N (0.02 mg L - 1 ). Laboratory microcosm incubations did not detect consistent N 2 production, despite experimental nitrate enrichment. Together, these results show that T. natans beds create seasonally hypoxic, nitrate-depleted conditions. However, weak and inconsistent N 2 production in our incubation experiments indicates that additional studies are needed to further assess the fate of nitrogen within T. natans beds and whether management may involve potential tradeoffs between habitat quality and nutrient cycling.

items.title: A Validated LNA ‐Modified Probe‐Based qPCR Assay for the Fast and Accurate Detection of the Root Rot Pathogen Phytophthora × cambivora on Mycelial DNA and Artificially Inoculated Chestnut Tissue
items.authors: Viola Papini, Alessandra Benigno, M. Moriconi, D. Rizzo, Salvatore Moricca, Francesco Bigazzi
items.abstract: Phytophthora × cambivora is a destructive, hybrid pathogen that has plagued European forests and agroforestry systems for at least two centuries. This polyphagous oomycete, known as the causal agent of ink disease, is responsible for the decline of chestnut forests and orchards, as well as beech and oak stands. Its widespread occurrence in nurseries, traded propagation material, soil, irrigation basins, puddles along forest tracks, and watercourses increases the risk of local and long‐distance spread. Traditional identification methods based on symptom assessment, baiting and isolation on selective media no longer meet modern diagnostic requirements because they are time‐consuming, require specialised mycological expertise and often lack sufficient sensitivity and specificity. Currently, there are few methods available that use real‐time PCR to detect and quantify the pathogen. A new quantitative real‐time PCR (qPCR) assay that uses a locked nucleic acid (LNA) probe has been developed and validated on artificially infected chestnut tissue to address this issue. Our assay targeted a mitochondrial intergenic region between the NAD7 and COX3 genes. The primers and probe were designed using the OligoArchitect software. Specificity assays tested the target against a wide range of oomycetes, with validation carried out according to EPPO standard PM7/98. This method detects low levels of P. × cambivora DNA in infected chestnut tissue with a detection limit of 600 fg/μL, close to that of purified DNA. This qPCR‐LNA assay offers a fast, specific and robust tool for pathogen detection in a variety of applications, including routine diagnostics in nurseries and other vulnerable settings.

items.title: The Effect of Tannin Powder Supplementation in the Ration on Hematological Profiles and Blood Urea Nitrogen of Priangan Sheep
items.authors: Najwa Hegyra Gumilar, I. Hernaman, D. Latipudin, Ghistavera Izvantika
items.abstract: The use of dietary tannins as natural feed additives to regulate rumen protein degradation and improve nitrogen metabolism has been increasingly explored. Nevertheless, the evidence concerning the combined use of chestnut (Castanea sativa) and quebracho (Schinopsis lorentzii) tannin extracts in Priangan sheep is still limited. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of a commercial tannin powder containing these two plant extracts on Blood Urea Nitrogen (BUN) concentration and hematological profiles in Priangan sheep. Eighteen healthy male Priangan sheep with an initial average body weight of 19.64±2.51 kg were randomly allocated into three dietary treatments in a Completely Randomized Design with six animals assigned to each treatment. The experimental diets consisted of a control ration (P0), control ration plus 1% tannin powder (P1) and control ration plus 2% tannin powder (P2). Blood samples were taken for biochemical and hematological evaluation after 70 days of feeding. 2% tannin powder supplementation significantly increased BUN concentration compared to control and 1% supplementation groups (P 0.05). In general, supplementation with chestnut and quebracho tannin powder at the 2% inclusion level induced alterations in nitrogen metabolism without any measurable changes in the hematological status. The results of this study suggest that the tannin preparation tested can be included in the diet of Priangan sheep at up to 2% of dietary dry matter without causing adverse physiological effects.

items.title: Chestnut starch-lipid complex as a nontraditional RS5 ingredient: Structural features and associated in vivo responses in high-fat diet-fed mice.
items.authors: Zhen-Ting Yu, Nan Ma, Fan Wei, Jin Deng, Hao-Xin Cui, Huan Lv
items.abstract: Resistant starch type 5 (RS5) can convert starch-rich crops into enzyme-resistant starch-lipid complexes, yet current evidence remains dominated by conventional starch sources and in vitro studies. This study prepared and characterized a chestnut starch-stearic acid complex (chestnut starch-lipid complex, DCS_C18, RS5), and evaluated it as a novel RS5 ingredient in high-fat diet (HFD)-fed mice, using native chestnut starch, caffeine, and orlistat as contextual comparators. DCS_C18 showed V-/B-type crystalline features, greater short-range and long-range order, and higher thermal stability than the palmitic acid complex. In vivo, DCS_C18 attenuated HFD-induced weight gain, adiposity, dyslipidemia, glucose intolerance, insulin resistance, hepatic steatosis, and systemic inflammation, accompanied by reduced lipogenic and increased fatty acid oxidation-related gene expression. Moreover, DCS_C18 exhibited more balanced regulation of fasting and postprandial glycemia than the other interventions. DCS_C18 also increased fecal acetate (2.12-fold) and butyrate (1.82-fold) and enriched SCFA-associated genera, including Blautia, Roseburia, and Lachnoclostridium. Open-field testing suggested improved locomotor and anxiety-related outcomes without the stimulant-like pattern observed for caffeine. These findings support chestnut-derived RS5 as a promising ingredient platform for metabolic-health-oriented foods, pending human and mechanistic confirmation.

items.title: Jujuboside A ameliorates T2DM-associated MASH: Suppression of YY1/FAS axis-mediated hepatic de novo fatty acid biosynthesis.
items.authors: Ting-Ting Yang, Li-Bang Chen, Hao-Nan Luo, Li-Ying Wang, Xi-Yan Jiang, Hao Yang
items.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) represents a progressive subtype of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), and is predominantly driven by dysregulated hepatic fatty acid (FA) metabolism. Although Jujuboside A (Ju A), a major bioactive triterpene saponin isolated from Ziziphus jujuba Mill. (sour jujube), exhibits hepatoprotective properties, its precise regulatory mechanisms underlying T2DM-associated MASH remain poorly defined. This study investigated the dose-dependent protective effects and molecular mechanisms of Ju A using both in vivo and in vitro models. Combining targeted FA profiling and long-chain FAs (LCFAs)-specific metabolomics, alongside chromatin immunoprecipitation (Ch-IP), luciferase reporter assays, molecular docking with dynamics simulations, and Yin Yang 1 (YY1) gain-of-function and fatty acid synthase (FAS) inhibition (C75) studies, we characterized Ju A-mediated metabolic reprogramming and molecular targets involved. Ju A treatment markedly ameliorated MASH and hepatic lipid deposition in diabetic mice by restoring dysregulated hepatic FA homeostasis, particularly by blocking de novo lipogenesis (DNL)-derived LCFA accumulation. Mechanistically, Ju A exerted these effects by blocking the nuclear translocation of YY1. This inhibition diminished YY1 binding to the FAS promoter, subsequently downregulating FAS expression and inhibiting aberrant hepatic de novo FA biosynthesis. Collectively, these findings demonstrated that Ju A ameliorated T2DM-associated MASH by restoring hepatic FA homeostasis via inactivation of the YY1-FAS axis, highlighting its promising therapeutic potential against diabetic liver complications.

items.title: Lipid and Secondary Metabolite Profile Changes During Cold Storage of Dongzao (Ziziphus jujuba Mill. cv. Dongzao): Responses to Postharvest Treatments and Implications for Marketability
items.authors: S. Yao, F. O. Holguin
items.abstract: Dongzao (Ziziphus jujuba Mill. cv. Dongzao) is a popular fresh-eating cultivar with a short shelf life at room temperature. As Dongzao acreage increases in the United States, extending the fresh-fruit supply window is important for commercial production. A preliminary study showed that Dongzao fruit began developing mold after approximately 5 weeks of cold storage. Therefore, a subsequent study evaluated the effects of an ethylene absorbent and two fungicides, Scholar and Mentor, on fruit quality, decay, and metabolomic changes during extended cold storage at 0 ± 0.5 °C. Compared with untreated fruit, the ethylene absorbent did not extend storage life or reduce decay, with more than 30% stem-end rot observed by week 6, suggesting that ethylene removal had limited effects on Dongzao storage deterioration. Both fungicides substantially reduced decay, but Scholar was more effective, with no stem-end rot detected after 9 weeks of storage. Heatmap and principal component analyses further showed that Scholar-treated fruit after 9 weeks clustered with fruit stored for 6 weeks, suggesting that Scholar treatment was associated with delayed metabolic changes accompanying advanced storage deterioration. Cold storage induced extensive lipid remodeling, with substantial increases in lipid metabolites, particularly lysophosphatidylcholines, lysophosphatidylethanolamines, and free fatty acids, indicating pronounced changes in membrane lipid metabolism under prolonged low-temperature storage. Cold storage also broadly altered secondary metabolism, including flavonoids, phenolic acids, alkaloids, and terpenoids. Although cold storage was the primary driver of metabolomic changes, Scholar treatment was associated with distinct alterations in flavonoid and terpenoid profiles after 9 weeks…

items.title: Free Amino Acid Composition in Various Organs, Fruit Maturity Stages, and Varieties of Jujube
items.authors: Chen Yang, Bi-Cong Li, Jin Yu, Xiao-Hua Yu, Ai-Ling Zhao, Xiao-Fang Xue
items.abstract: Jujubes ( Ziziphus jujuba Mill.) are rich in a variety of nutrients, among which free amino acids are important indicators, reflecting their nutritional quality and functional value. We investigated the dynamic changes in free amino acid contents during jujube fruit ripening, analyzed the differences among different organs and varieties, and provide a scientific basis for the quality evaluation and comprehensive utilization of amino acids in jujubes. Free amino acid contents in different jujube organs (fruit, flower, leaf), at five different developmental stages, and in the fruit of eight jujube varieties were determined using an automatic amino acid analyzer. Twelve free amino acids were detected in all tested samples, with total contents ranging from 50.35 to 76.26 mg/100 g fresh weight (FW). In terms of dynamic changes, in general the total free amino acid contents in fruit of the four varieties showed a decreasing trend and then an increase during ripening. Specifically, the total content was highest at the young fruit stage and second highest at the full-red stage in ‘Beijingsuanzao’. It was highest at the full-red stage and second greatest at the half-red stage in ‘Huanghuadongzao’, ‘Xinzhenghuizao’, and ‘Tailihong’. The total content was lowest at the expansion stage in ‘Tailihong’, but lowest at the white-ripe stage in the other three varieties. In terms of organ differences, the total free amino acid content in different organs followed the order fruit > flower > leaf. For varietal differences, the total free amino acid content in eight jujube varieties at the crisp-ripe stage differed significantly, ranging from 154.89 to 544.46 mg/100 g FW. items.title: A Comparison of Two Species-Discriminatory SNP Sets for Taxonomic Assignment in Hybridizing European White Oaks (Quercus sect. Quercus).
items.authors: Rellstab C, Guichoux E, Gugerli F, Kremer A, Reutimann O.
items.abstract: Species identification is essential for conservation, forest management, and understanding ecological and evolutionary dynamics, such as adaptive introgression and maintenance of species boundaries in hybridizing taxa. Species-discriminatory marker sets have been shown to be more accurate than morphological identification, especially in hybridizing species complexes, and provide a more affordable alternative to genome-wide analyses. However, to our knowledge, no species complex exists for which several marker sets are available, let alone have been compared to each other. Moreover, it remains unclear how well marker sets can be applied to additional, closely related species. Here, we compared two independently developed SNP sets, one derived from amplicon sequencing and one from whole-genome sequencing, for three morphologically similar and hybridizing European white oak species sensu lato (Quercus robur, Q. petraea, and Q. pubescens). We applied the SNP sets to 560 samples, including samples of known pure ancestry, controlled crosses, natural populations, and four additional white oak species. Congruency between SNP sets was very high, but species assignment was slightly more accurate for the reference samples used in the development of the respective SNP set. Ancestry coefficients for first-generation hybrids were more precise with the SNP set based on whole-genome data. In a natural population, there was limited congruency between SNP sets in quantifying admixture. Notably, the SNP sets were able to identify up to two additional white oak species. Our study highlights the great potential of species-discriminatory SNP sets in science and practice, while demonstrating that ascertainment bias should not be neglected, and accurate introgression assessments may require ge…

items.title: Repurposing of traditional Siddha drug for external application in chronic irritant contact dermatitis – A case report
items.authors: Ulagamadhavan Muthuraj
items.abstract: Siddha system of medicine offers several drugs for managing skin disorders, including contact dermatitis. Hence, a maiden attempt was made to repurpose an internal medicine for external application in chronic irritant contact dermatitis. A 30-year-old tea vendor with an 8-year history was treated with the drug, containing chestnut as its chief ingredient and occupational avoidance for 14 days. Complete resolution of dermatitis and symptoms was observed, with no recurrence during 12 months of drugless follow-up. However, well-designed clinical trials are required to evaluate its efficacy.

items.title: Genome-Wide Identification and Expression Analysis of ZjCDPK Genes Related to Ripening of ‘Dongzao’ Jujube Fruit
items.authors: Bing-Xin Fan, Huang Li, Shi-Xing Wang, Su-Na Zhao, Zhao-Kun Zhi, Shu-Lin Zhang
items.abstract: Calcium-dependent protein kinases (CDPKs) are plant-specific Ca2+ sensors that translate calcium signals into phosphorylation responses. CDPKs coordinate both plant responses to the environment and plant growth, including fruit development and ripening. However, the CDPK gene family and its potential roles in jujube fruit development remain poorly characterized. In this study, 19 ZjCDPK genes were identified in the genome of ‘winter jujube’ (Ziziphus jujuba Mill. cv. ‘Dongzao’) and mapped to 11 of the 12 chromosomes. Phylogenetic analysis classified the ZjCDPK proteins into four groups, with CDPKs from Arabidopsis and tomato. Two intraspecific collinear gene pairs and sixteen orthologous gene pairs between ‘Dongzao’ and Arabidopsis were identified. Most family members exhibited similar organization of exon–intron splicing and contained similar motifs, with all containing a conserved serine/threonine protein kinase catalytic domain and four C-terminal EF-hand motifs. Promoter analysis identified 681 cis-acting elements, with abundant elements associated with abiotic stress, light, and phytohormone responses, including those related to abscisic acid, ethylene, methyl jasmonate, salicylic acid, auxin, and gibberellin. Developmental expression profiling across seven fruit stages, together with qRT-PCR validation, showed that ZjCDPK02, 08, 10, 12, 14, 16, and 19 accumulated preferentially during the late stages of fruit development. Correlation analysis further showed that ZjCDPK14 was strongly co-expressed with ZjCDPK02 (r = 0.96) and positively correlated with both fruit firmness (r = 0.907) and total soluble solids content (r = 0.816). Significant associations with these quality traits were also detected for ZjCDPK02, 04, 08, 15, 16, and 19. These findings provide a compr…

items.title: Bezoars-Induced Small Bowel Obstructions due to Dried Persimmons that Required Multiple Surgeries: A Case Report
items.authors: Yoshikuni Yonenaga, Ryota Ito
items.abstract: ABSTRACT INTRODUCTION A bezoar is an indigestible conglomeration trapped in the gastrointestinal tract. Persimmon phytobezoars, known as diospyrobezoars, are formed after the frequent consumption of persimmons and are a distinct type of phytobezoar characterized by their hard consistency. CASE PRESENTATION A 74-year-old female presented to our hospital with persistent abdominal pain and vomiting, and an intestinal strangulating obstruction was suspected. An emergency operation was performed, and a dietary small bowel obstruction was diagnosed. A small intestinal resection, including removal of a foreign body resembling a sponge-like mass, was performed. During detailed questioning, we asked her about any history of persimmon ingestion, but she denied it. The symptoms recurred on POD 8, and another dietary small bowel obstruction was suspected after a CT examination. Conservative treatment, including Coca-Cola dissolution therapy, was performed, but the symptoms were not alleviated, and she developed a fever on POD 24. On POD 30—the 22nd day after the 2nd onset—she suddenly remembered that she had eaten 16 dried persimmons between 24 and 19 days before the onset of symptoms. A 2nd operation was performed the following day. Because feces were found in the abdominal cavity and the perforated site could not be found laparoscopically, we converted to laparotomy. At the location of the obstruction in the ileum, a foreign body and a perforation were seen, and a partial ileectomy was performed. The foreign body also resembled a sponge-like mass, and a component analysis showed that it consisted of 98% tannin. A diospyrobezoar was finally diagnosed. items.title: Blackberry Leaf Blotch Virus, a Novel Emaravirus Infecting Cultivated and Wild Blackberry Plants in Europe.
items.authors: Hellin P, Richet P, Demonty E, de Koning PPM, de Krom C, den Hartog WGSA, Westenberg M, Botermans M, Druciarek T, Winter S, Rimbaud L, Dubuis N, Blouin AG, Kovačec E, Grubar B, Toplak N, Steyer S, Mav
items.abstract: A novel emaravirus provisionally named blackberry leaf blotch virus (BLBV), was identified from cultivated and wild blackberry plants ( Rubus sp.) exhibiting leaf blotch and vein banding/feathering symptoms. BLBV has been detected in Belgium, France, the Netherlands and Slovenia. The virus is most closely related to raspberry leaf blotch virus (RLBV, Emaravirus idaeobati ) infecting raspberry ( Rubus idaeus ) in Europe, and is distant from blackberry leaf mottle-associated virus (BLMaV, Emaravirus rubi ), infecting blackberry in the USA. Up to eight RNA segments were identified in BLBV isolates, including the four core RNA segments present in all emaraviruses and up to four additional non-core RNA segments. Spherical virus-like particles (70-90 nm), morphologically similar to emaravirus virions, were observed in sap from symptomatic blackberry tissue by transmission electron microscopy. The proteins encoded by the core RNA segments were all more than 20% divergent from their closest known emaravirus homologues, supporting the classification of BLBV as a new species. Genetic diversity was found among isolates even at the country level, with some additional RNA segments only detected for some isolates. Eriophyoid mites, known vectors of emaraviruses, were found on several infected plants and molecular barcoding identified the them as Epitrimerus gibbosus , an eriophyoid species previously reported on Rubus spp. in Europe. Transmission bioassays performed with these mites in a greenhouse supported E. gibbosus as a putative vector of BLBV. This discovery raises questions about the impact of BLBV on blackberry crops and the need for virus surveillance in plant propagation material.

items.title: Combined effects of drought and insect herbivory on oak leaf endophytic communities and performance.
items.authors: Barlier T, Castagneyrol B, Carton J, Burlett R, Bonnard O, Schimann H.
items.abstract: Leaf-associated microbiota are considered sensitive indicators of how plants respond to their environment. Yet, plants can be exposed to a wide range of biotic and abiotic stresses whose independent and combined effects on plant microbiota remain poorly understood, as do their cumulative consequences for plant performance. We conducted an experiment to expose saplings of four oak species to drought and herbivory by a piercing-sucking insect. We assessed the effect of water deficit on herbivory, as well as the individual and combined effects of water deficit and herbivory on fungal endophytic communities. To evaluate the cumulative impacts of biotic and abiotic stresses on plant performance, and the potential of the fungal endophytic communities as an indicator of plant responses to stress, we measured photosynthetic capacity, growth, and the accumulation of non-structural carbohydrates in twigs at the end of the growing season. Water deficit had no effect on insect herbivory but induced a decrease in the diversity of the leaf-associated fungal community. In contrast, herbivory shifted the composition of fungal communities through species replacement or addition depending on oak species. Herbivory altered photosynthesis, whereas drought but not herbivory reduced oak growth. None of these stresses influenced the storage of non-structural carbohydrates. Leaf-associated fungi responded to both stresses. However, the underlying mechanisms appeared to differ and the association with oak performance was weak. Overall, our study suggests a certain degree of resilience in trees subjected to interacting stresses, while also highlighting vulnerabilities that may have implications for tree health over the long term.

items.title: Seasonal variation in Korean school lunch menus using big data from the National Education Information System: an exploratory study.
items.authors: Shin J, Park E.
items.abstract: School meal programs in South Korea are a major public nutrition service and an important part of student diets. Although previous National Education Information System- based studies have described frequently served menu items and annual trends, nationwide evidence on how school lunch menus differ seasonally remains limited. Thus, in this exploratory study, we aimed to analyze summer-winter differences in frequently served items in South Korean elementary, middle, and high schools. Nationwide school lunch records from 2023 to 2025 were obtained from the National School Meal Information application programming interface. Lunch meal units served in elementary, middle, and high schools were analyzed. The final dataset comprised 1,200,000 meal units. Menu items were classified into six categories: rice/noodles, soups/stews, kimchi, main dishes, side dishes, and desserts. In each category, items frequently served in summer and winter were identified, and seasonal differences were quantified using a seasonal gap index and z-tests. Seasonal variation was highest in kimchi and desserts. Among the top items, 25/26 kimchi items and 27/30 dessert items showed significant seasonal differences. In desserts, watermelon, oriental melon, and ice cream were strongly summer-dominant, whereas apple, strawberry, and sweet persimmon were winter-dominant. In kimchi, young summer radish kimchi and cucumber kimchi were summer-dominant, whereas diced radish kimchi and napa cabbage kimchi were winter-dominant. Rice/noodles, soups/stews, and side dishes showed moderate seasonal variation. Main dishes showed the lowest degree of seasonal variation, with all-time popular items displaying minimal variation. items.title: Profiling of pollen in honey using multispectral imaging flow cytometry.
items.authors: Walther F, Hofmann M, Janke M, Erler S, Friedrich E, Treder M, Rakosy D, Harpole WS, Mäder P, Berdún A, Hornick T, Dunker S.
items.abstract: Pollen identification from honey (melissopalynology) is of great economic and consumer relevance. Traditional microscopy is time-consuming and dependent on expert knowledge, thus limiting high-throughput analyses. We tested whether pollen images generated with Multispectral Imaging Flow Cytometry (MIFC) classified by machine learning (ML) (convolution neural networks (CNNs) and random forest (RF)) can serve as a fast and reproducible method for identifying pollen in honey. We examined how the classification of honey pollen is affected by images from different matrices (anther and honey samples), how results compare with traditional microscopic analysis and used a set of human-interpretable image features to better explain ML results. The study focused on the six common target pollen in honey Brassica, Castanea, Centaurea, Helianthus, Phacelia and Tilia type. A classifier trained with a combination of anther and honey brightfield and fluorescence images provided the best predictions for 13 monofloral and 10 polyfloral honeys. Yielding pollen identification results comparable to microscopy, three times more pollen can be evaluated, and a measurement time of a maximum of 10 min, the method demonstrates its high potential as a powerful screening tool in melissopalynology.

items.title: Effects of individual and combined plant-extract treatments on the mechanical properties of sheepskin leather
items.authors: M. Mels, B. Bitlisli, L. Sarttarova, Bekzhan Abzalbekuly, Jakhongir Gafurov, A. Tortay
items.abstract: The object of the study was the technology of treating sheepskin leather intended for footwear manufacture with natural plant extracts, with particular attention to its mechanical performance. The problem was to select a binary treatment that would balance tensile strength, tear resistance, and elongation at break, because these properties do not necessarily respond in the same way to increasing extract concentration. The study examined chrome-tanned sheepskin leather treated with plant extracts for potential use as a footwear material. Individual oak bark, agrimony, horse chestnut, and chlorophyll treatments and binary combinations were first compared. Oak bark and horse chestnut extracts were then studied at concentrations of 1.5–2.5% each. Regression models and multi-response optimization were used to examine concentration-dependent changes and select a treatment condition within this range. Oak bark gave the highest tensile strength among the individual treatments, whereas the oak bark–horse chestnut combination gave the highest tear resistance among the screened treatments. In the concentration experiment, higher oak bark levels favored tensile strength, tear resistance showed a curved response to horse chestnut concentration, and elongation decreased towards higher extract concentrations. A treatment with 2.0% oak bark and 2.25% horse chestnut was selected as a compromise among the three responses (overall desirability 0.65697). At this condition, experimental tensile strength, tear resistance, and elongation were 8.605 ± 0.17 N/mm2, 40.707 ± 0.81 N/mm, and 48.725 ± 0.97%, respectively. items.title: Phenotypic Characterization and Transcriptomic Profiling of Ziziphus jujuba var. spinosa Seedlings Under ATP Treatment and Identification of a Novel Lupeol Synthase
items.authors: Yan-Sheng Wu, Shen-Xiu Du, Hua-Liang Liu, Yi-Mian Ma, Wen-Jing Wang, Ye-Lin Tian
items.abstract: The tender leaves of Ziziphus jujuba var. spinosa (sour jujube) are widely consumed in China as a health-promoting tea, with triterpenoids being identified as one of their core bioactive constituents. However, key genes in the triterpenoid biosynthesis pathway remain largely uncharacterized in this species. Here, adenosine triphosphate (ATP) treatment inhibited sour jujube seedling growth, induced leaf curling and marginal withering in partial seedlings, and elevated triterpenoid content in seedling aboveground tissues. Transcriptome analysis showed that most mevalonic acid (MVA) pathway enzyme genes were not significantly altered, while some were downregulated, and some enzyme isoforms were slightly upregulated. Combined genome and transcriptome analysis identified one slightly upregulated oxidosqualene cyclase (OSC) gene, ZsLUS, among 13 sour jujube OSC family genes. Heterologous expression in yeast confirmed that ZsLUS encodes a bona fide lupeol synthase with catalytic activity. These results indicate that ATP treatment enhances triterpenoid accumulation without uniformly upregulating MVA pathway genes, suggesting a sub-pathway-specific regulatory mode or post-transcriptional regulatory mechanism for triterpenoid biosynthesis in sour jujube seedlings. This work deepens our understanding of the mechanism of ATP action on sour jujube triterpenoid biosynthesis and provides new clues for deciphering triterpenoid biosynthesis and accumulation in sour jujube leaves.

items.title: Sirdaryo viloyati sharoitida chilonjiydaning istiqbolli navlari ko'chatlarini yetishtirish texnologiyasini takomillashtirish
items.authors: Jasur Eshquvvatov
items.abstract: This article analyzes the scientific basis for improving the technology of growing seedlings of promising jujube (Ziziphus jujuba Mill.) cultivars under the conditions of the Syrdarya region of Uzbekistan. The relevance of the study is associated with the adaptability of jujube to arid and continental climatic conditions, the nutritional and biological value of its fruits, and the increasing interest in expanding jujube cultivation in Uzbekistan. Scientific information on jujube cultivars introduced into Uzbekistan, seed and vegetative propagation methods, pre-sowing seed treatments, cutting rooting, and grafting techniques used for the production of planting material is reviewed. Previous research conducted under Uzbek conditions investigated nine jujube cultivars introduced from China, including Xiangzao, Zanhuangdazao, Tangzao, Mayabaizao, Junzao, Dabailing, Dongzao, Linyilizao, and Jixinzao, with several cultivars demonstrating promising adaptability. Recent research on seed propagation has also demonstrated the importance of pre-sowing treatment and sowing depth. Under the conditions of the Republic of Karakalpakstan, the highest seed germination was observed at a sowing depth of 2.5–3.0 cm, while scarification accelerated seed germination and improved germination performance. Studies of vegetative propagation have demonstrated that indole-3-butyric acid (IBA) can significantly improve the rooting of jujube cuttings and root development characteristics. The reviewed scientific evidence provides a basis for developing an adapted technology for producing high-quality jujube planting material under the soil and climatic conditions of the Syrdarya region.

items.title: Legal Challenges in the Registration of Farmers' Varieties under the Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers' Rights Act, 2001
items.journal: International Journal of Law Management & Humanities
items.authors: V. M. Kandiyar
items.abstract: The Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers’ Rights Act, 2001 (PPV&FR Act) is the intellectual property framework developed by India to protect plant varieties while taking into account the role of farmers in agricultural innovation and the conservation of biodiversity. However, many problems remain in the registration of farmers’ varieties. This paper examines whether the existing registration regime is able to protect traditional farmers’ varieties, given that the registration system is predominantly based on formal and standardized plant variety protection. The main emphasis is on the problems farmers face in fulfilling the criteria of distinctiveness, uniformity and stability (DUS) when traditional varieties contain genetic diversity and have developed over generations of farmers. The procedural, technical, evidential and financial problems of registration are also analyzed, along with the question whether small farmers can fulfill all the requirements. The paper further discusses the limited time period for the registration of farmers’ varieties. It also explores the role of traditional farmers in the plant variety protection regime, especially traditional farmers who have conserved, developed or improved such traditional varieties and may also be recognized as breeders. The recognition of such farmers as breeders raises issues about the kind of rights they hold as breeders and the possible conflict between their rights as traditional farmers and their rights under plant variety protection. The study asks whether the present regime properly balances the intellectual property rights of farmers as breeders, on the one hand, and their traditional practices of cultivating, using, exchanging and conserving plant varieties, on the other.

items.title: A new species of the genus Dysommina from the Lakshadweep Sea, India (Anguilliformes: Synaphobranchidae: Ilyophinae).
items.authors: Kodeeswaran P.
items.abstract: This study describes a new Dysommina species, based on two specimens collected at a depth of ca. 600 m in the Lakshadweep Sea off south-western India. The new species differs from its congeners in having fewer total vertebrae (120-127 vs. 134 in D. castanea, 133-134 in D. brevis, and 137-141 in D. orientalis), fewer predorsal vertebrae (14-15 vs. 16 in D. pygmaea), fewer preanal vertebrae (24-27 vs. 28-31 in D. rugosa), and in a combination of morphometric, meristic, dentition and colouration characters. DNA sequences were generated and analysed.

items.title: Somatic embryogenesis from leaf segments of Quercus castanea Mill.
items.authors: C. Castillo-Martínez, E. Velasco-Bautista, M. Vallejo-Reyna, M. T. González-Arnao, Lizbeth Fernández-Cruz
items.abstract: Objective: To evaluate the capacity of leaf segments obtained from young shoots collected from adult Quercus castanea Mill. trees to form embryogenic callus and somatic embryos under in vitro conditions. Design/methodology/approach: The study was conducted in two stages. In the first stage, two culture media were compared to induce embryogenic callus and somatic embryos from leaf segments. In the second stage, the medium that produced the best response was evaluated under two incubation conditions, light and darkness, to determine their effect on callus growth and somatic embryo development. Results: In the first stage, WPM medium supplemented with 0.5 mg L⁻¹ 2,4-D showed the best response, with 82% embryogenic callus formation and 32% somatic embryo formation. In the second stage, no statistically significant differences were detected between light and darkness, indicating that these conditions did not substantially did not significantly affect callus volume.. Somatic embryos maturation reached 95%after transfer to MS medium without growth regulators and supplemented with 100 mg L⁻¹ polyvinylpyrrolidone. Limitations/implications: The study was conducted under controlled in vitro culture conditions and focused on the response of leaf explants obtained from young shoots of adult trees; therefore, further studies are required to strengthen the protocol and evaluate its reproducibility under broader experimental conditions. Findings/conclusions: Leaf segments of Q. castanea constitute a viable source of explants for the induction of somatic embryogenesis. WPM medium supplemented with 2,4-D promoted embryogenic callus induction and somatic embryo formation, whereas incubation under light or darkness did not significantly modify the response.

items.title: The Relationship of Cultivars, Structures and In Vitro Digestibility of Chinese Chestnut (Castanea henryi) Starches Treated with Low-Voltage Electrostatic Field Technology
items.authors: Feng Chen, Xian-Tong Wu, Wen-Can Luo, Jing Wang, Wei-Jing Zhuang, Wen-Sheng Chen
items.abstract: Low-voltage electrostatic field (LVEF) treatment is an emerging food preservation technology that exploits the physical effects of electrostatic fields; however, its mechanisms of action in nut crops remain poorly understood. This study investigated changes in starch structure, processing properties, and in vitro digestibility in five chestnut cultivars (Castanea henryi) from different regions of China (Chushuhong, Changmangzi, Youzhen, Hongzhenzi, and Huangzhen) following refrigeration treatment (RT) and LVEF treatment. LVEF increased the crystallinity and molecular order of chestnut starch. It also generally reduced free water content, peak viscosity (PV), breakdown viscosity (BV), and setback viscosity (SV), while increasing water-holding capacity. In addition, LVEF enhanced the resistance to shear and retrogradation, thereby improving starch processing performance. The TPA results showed that LVEF improved the textural properties of chestnut starch gels, supporting their suitability for gel-based foods. The responses varied among the cultivars. Compared with RT, LVEF reduced the particle size and free water content of Chushuhong starch by 19.56% and 18.41%, respectively. Chushuhong also exhibited the largest increase in crystallinity (31.34%), while the bound water content of its starch gel increased by 13.70%, indicating stronger responsiveness to LVEF. Overall, LVEF improved the processing performance of chestnut starch, although varietal differences in the responses were observed. LVEF-treated Chushuhong and Changmangzi starches exhibited favorable processing properties, indicating their suitability for developing processed chestnut products. Meanwhile, their starches exhibited faster enzymatic hydrolysis rates under in vitro conditions. These findings provide a …

items.title: Organic Acids and Bacterial Communities of Backslopped Sourdough Prepared with Japanese Pear (Pyrus pyrifolia Nakai) Infusion
items.authors: Riho Endo, Tsukasa Shiraishi, Mihoko Moto
items.abstract: Addition of fruit during sourdough preparation can lead to the development of distinctive bacterial communities and fermentation characteristics. However, sourdough preparation with Japanese pear infusion remains understudied. We prepared sourdough with Japanese pear infusion and evaluated its organic acid composition and bacterial community. Sourdough was passaged for up to 56 generations. pH decreased rapidly during the initial generations of backslopping and subsequently stabilized at 3.5 and 3.7. High-performance liquid chromatography analysis revealed that lactic and acetic acid were the major organic acids. The fermentation quotient in the 55th and 56th generations ranged from 0.64 to 0.70, indicating an acetic acid-dominant profile. Bacterial community analysis targeting the V3–V4 region of the 16S rDNA gene revealed Furfurilactobacillus rossiae and Acetobacter pasteurianus as the dominant taxa. Average nucleotide identity analysis identified the representative isolates as Furfurilactobacillus milii and Acetobacter pasteurianus subsp. pasteurianus, respectively. This descriptive study is limited by a small sample size, lack of a control group, initial bacterial community data, and limited statistical analysis. Nevertheless, under the experimental conditions of this study, relatively high acetic acid levels were observed in the analyzed sourdoughs, together with a bacterial community dominated by the genera Furfurilactobacillus and Acetobacter were observed as predominant genera.

items.title: Comparative genomic analysis for selected members of the Ophiostomatales: insights into biosynthetic gene clusters and CAZymes.
items.authors: Abed S, Kumar A, Hausner G.
items.abstract: The Order Ophiostomatales includes ecologically diverse fungi, and many are associates of bark and/or ambrosia beetles. This order includes species that cause tree diseases, and many members are sapwood staining fungi. Despite their ecological and economic importance, the genomic basis of their adaptations remains poorly understood. Here, we present annotated genome assemblies for six species (seven strains) spanning three genera within the Ophiostomatales. Genomes ranged from 21 to 32 Mb with high completeness scores. CAZyme analyses revealed broadly conserved repertoires dominated by glycoside hydrolases and glycosyltransferases, with substantial representation of lignin-and cellulose-associated enzymes and marked quantitative variation among taxa, including expanded oxidative auxiliary activity families in Ophiostoma quercus and Leptographium truncatum and a reduced profile in Ceratocystiopsis minima. antiSMASH predicted 12-19 biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) among the seven genomes. Rather than only broad metabolite classes, comparative analysis revealed conservation of specific secondary metabolite families, including a putative 1,8-dihydroxynaphthalene (DHN) melanin cluster present in all genomes, a conserved fujikurin-like type I polyketide synthase (T1PKS) cluster present in all genomes except L. truncatum, and an Ophiostoma-specific NRPSbased metallophore/siderophore-like cluster potentially involved in iron acquisition. The genomic data provide new insights into the metabolic capacity and potential ecological differentiation of the Ophiostomatales.

items.title: Comparative Analyses of the Organellar Genomes of Quercus Reveal Contrasting Evolutionary Dynamics
items.authors: Si-Nuo Feng, Yu Li, Yi-Gang Song
items.abstract: Background: Mitochondrial and chloroplast genomes in plants have experienced distinct evolutionary trajectories due to differences in genomic organization, functional constraints, and genome maintenance mechanisms. However, comparative studies of their evolutionary dynamics in oaks remain limited. Methods: The complete mitochondrial and chloroplast genomes of Quercus arbutifolia were assembled and annotated using PacBio HiFi reads. Genome structure, repetitive sequences, codon usage, and mitochondrial plastid DNA transfers (MTPTs) were characterized. Results: The mitochondrial genome of Q. arbutifolia was assembled as a 493,735 bp linear molecule, whereas the chloroplast genome was assembled as a 160,682 bp circular molecule. items.title: Testing the Potential of <i>Pseudomonas</i> Bacteria for the Biocontrol of Ink Disease of Chestnut.
items.authors: Dennert F, Troxler V, Bossert OX, Schneider S, Maurhofer M, Prospero S.
items.abstract: Ink disease, caused by the two oomycetes Phytophthora cinnamomi and Phytophthora × cambivora , is one of the most devastating diseases of sweet chestnut ( Castanea sativa ) in Europe. Its control is particularly difficult, with few fungicides showing a satisfactory effect, and those being progressively banned in forest ecosystems or in forest-like plantations because of ecological concerns. Therefore, alternative, nature-friendly control methods are urgently needed. The bacterial genus Pseudomonas includes many species with antifungal and antimicrobial properties. In this study, we isolated Pseudomonas bacteria from the rhizosphere of healthy and diseased chestnut trees in southern Switzerland. Out of 166 isolated Pseudomonas strains, 5 showed significant growth inhibition of P . cinnamomi and/or P . × cambivora in vitro. Three strains that significantly inhibited the growth of both pathogens were tested against a collection of 20 isolates of each species, showing that the in vitro inhibition is independent of the pathogen isolate. The mechanisms underlying this inhibition remain unclear because none of the three strains harbored biosynthesis genes coding for well-known antimicrobial secondary metabolites. Phylogenetic analysis of whole genome sequences showed that two of the strains belong to the P . fluorescens subgroup, whereas one strain probably belongs to a previously unrecognized species closely related to the P . putida subgroup. The results of this study indicate that Pseudomonas have the potential to be used as biocontrol agents against ink disease. Further experiments are needed to confirm their inhibitory effect against P . cinnamomi and P . × cambivora in vivo.

items.title: Identification and Expression Profiling of Olfactory-Related Genes in Exolontha castanea (Coleoptera: Melolonthinae) Using Tissue-Specific Transcriptomics
items.authors: Wen-Jing He, Yu-Xin Yang, Cheng-Hua Huang, Xue-Hong Pan, Gen Xia, Zi-Xuan Wu
items.abstract: Exolontha castanea is an important subterranean pest of sugarcane in China, currently controlled mainly by chemical insecticides. However, prolonged and improperly timed insecticide application has exacerbated infestations, necessitating the development of eco-friendly management strategies. Given the pivotal role of olfactory-related genes in host-seeking, mating, and oviposition, deciphering the olfactory mechanisms of E. castanea may support environmentally sound pest management. In this study, we sequenced transcriptomes from different tissues of male and female E. castanea and annotated olfactory-related genes. We identified 35 odorant binding proteins (OBPs), 12 chemosensory proteins (CSPs), 51 odorant receptors (ORs), 21 ionotropic receptors (IRs), and 4 sensory neuron membrane proteins (SNMPs). Expression profiling indicated that 13 OBPs, 6 CSPs, 16 ORs, 5 IRs, and 2 SNMPs were moderately or highly expressed in the antennae, and among these, 4 OBPs, 4 CSPs, 1 IR and 1 SNMP were also moderately or highly expressed in non-olfactory tissues. In addition, 8 OBPs, 1 CSP, 5 IRs and 1 SNMP displayed moderate or high expression levels only in non-olfactory tissues, including the head, leg, thorax, and abdomen. Based on these findings, the potential functions of these olfactory-related genes are discussed. This study represents the first comprehensive catalog of olfactory-related genes in E. castanea, laying a solid foundation for future functional characterization and novel sustainable pest management strategy development.

items.title: Research on Image Enhancement of Crisp-Ripe Stage Red Jujube Based on Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm
items.authors: Qi-Hang Yuan, Long Wang, Lu Shi, Qiao-Nan Yang, Yong-De Zhang
items.abstract: Machine vision technology plays a crucial role in non-destructive detection and online monitoring of deep processing for red dates during the crisp-ripe stage. However, due to factors such as uneven illumination in the collection environment and illumination attenuation on the curved surface of quasi-spherical objects, the collected images of red dates during the crisp-ripe stage often suffer from issues such as low overall image quality, difficulty in recognizing epidermal fruit spots and fine textures, low contrast between fruit surface crack defects and normal fruit surfaces, and blurred fruit body edges, which increase the difficulty of accurately identifying fruit surface features. In response to the common problems of over-enhancement and loss of details in current image enhancement methods when processing images of red dates during the crisp-ripe stage, this paper combines the practical requirements of preserving details of the fruit body and crack edges, enhancing epidermal texture clarity, balancing contrast and noise, and constructs a multi-dimensional image enhancement fitness function. A method for enhancing images of red dates during the crisp-ripe stage based on the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm is proposed. Through comparative experiments on image enhancement of red dates during the crisp-ripe stage, the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed image enhancement method are verified from both subjective visual effects and objective evaluation indicators.

items.title: Constructing restructured jujube using blackened jujube pulp and carrageenan to resolve Peel-induced rough mouthfeel.
items.authors: Zhang H, Wang Y, Sun X, Gao L, Zhang D, Zhang R.
items.abstract: Blackened jujube offers improved nutritional value, while its peel-induced coarse mouthfeel limits its broader use in snack-style products. To address this limitation, this study proposes restructuring blackened jujube pulp into self-supporting composite gels using κ-carrageenan (KC). While neither 0.5% KC nor the pulp alone formed a self-supporting gel, composite gels containing 0.5% KC were observed to be self-supporting, indicating that the pulp matrix facilitates gelation at a lower KC level. Increasing KC from 0.5% to 2.5% progressively strengthened the network, increasing hardness from ~2.5 N to 16.7 N, water-holding capacity from 53.45% to 77.01%, and freeze-thaw syneresis from 68.94% to 26.69%, alongside network densification and T₂₂ shortening (75.8 to 37.0 ms). Sensory evaluation also confirmed that restructuring markedly reduced grittiness and improved overall mouthfeel. Overall, this work offers a practical strategy for converting fruit pulps into self-supporting composite gels, thereby enabling blackened jujube products with tunable texture and improved mouthfeel. The authors contributed equally to this work.

The experiment was conducted in a randomised block design with three replications. A considerable amount of variability was detected for the studied vegetative, floral and corm traits with genotypes showing maximum variation for 21 traits comprising three continuous variables: plant height, corm weight before and after storage which subsequently contributed maximum to variability, that is, 4.24%, 4.23% and 4.35% respectively along dimension 1, and several categorical variables with anther: colour of stomium (6.09%) and outer bract: anthocyanin colouration (5.91%) as key contributors along dimension 2, as confirmed by factor analysis of mixed data (FAMD). items.authors: Aman Mahajan, A. Rana, J. Jyoti, Yogendra Kumar, Rama Kant, Ashok Kumar
items.abstract: Azadirachta indica A. Juss. (neem) is a multipurpose tree species of agricultural, medicinal, pesticidal and industrial importance. Increasing demand for neem-derived products, particularly neem oil for neem-coated urea, has stimulated genetic improvement programme for development of superior planting material with enhanced production and biochemical traits. In this context, Forest Research Institute (FRI), Dehradun, in collaboration with the Indian Farmers Fertiliser Cooperative Limited (IFFCO), released six elite neem varieties characterized by early flowering and fruiting, with oil content ranging from 35.44 to 43.51% and azadirachtin content from 6047 to 9760 ppm. The development and release of such improved varieties necessitate reliable and standardized distinctness, uniformity and stability (DUS) characterization for their identification, registration and legal protection. However, application of DUS testing in neem is challenging because of its perennial growth habit, extended juvenile phase, phenotypic plasticity and environmental influence on morphological traits. This systematic review synthesizes available information on DUS characterization in neem and critically examines morphological, quantitative, pseudo-qualitative and biochemical descriptors used for varietal identification. It identifies limitations in existing descriptor framework and highlights need for systematic validation across environments and developmental stages. Importantly, review contextualizes neem DUS characterization within recent advances in varietal development and considers its broader utility in breeding, germplasm characterization, conservation, and variety protection. items.title: Construction of China’s Legal Protection System for New Animal Varieties
items.authors: F. Chong
items.abstract: While new animal breeds have long been at the center of advancing both animal husbandry and the broader bioeconomy, there is considerable confusion regarding their legal protection in China. While the Patent Law specifically excludes the patenting of new animal varieties, the Animal Husbandry Law has historically focused upon administrative approvals of breeds rather than the establishment of proprietary rights. For this reason, it is not surprising that a gap exists in the law, since breeders of new animal varieties (novel, distinct, uniform, and stable) currently lack an exclusive civil right that may be established, sold, or enforced. This paper considers the experience of the EU under the Biotech Directive and the U.S. dual regulatory model in protecting biotechnological innovations involving non-human animals. Drawing upon an analysis of both systems, it proposes a multi-tiered protection system for new animal breeds in China. It is argued that China needs to break free from the current binary division between protected/unprotected animal varieties versus patentable/unpatentable inventions derived from animals. The proposed multi-tiered protection system for new animal breeds is based on the level of technological intervention involved, along with the level of ethical concerns raised by each type of new animal variety. Animals bred using genetic editing techniques that do not involve the introduction of foreign DNA – and therefore represent lower risk from an ethical standpoint – should be protected through a sui generis Animal Breeder’s Right modeled on the existing Plant Variety Protection system.
